comparison: Perfect agreement on claims C49-C55 regarding PV interneuron findings. Both evaluations find the evidence convincing that there are no differences in inhibitory transmission, PV interneuron counts, or PV cell intrinsic excitability. Reviewers explicitly noted this as 'novel and valuable.'

Perfect agreement on claims C75-C76, C81 regarding open field locomotor activity. Both evaluations accept the findings of normal locomotion with increased center entries. These served as important controls for repetitive behavior findings.

Perfect agreement on claims C97-C103 summarizing variable effects across brain regions and cell types. Both evaluations accept the discussion of Kv1.2 channel mechanisms and the synthesis of findings from current and prior literature.
Strong agreement on claims C86-C88 regarding enhanced motor learning on rotarod. Both evaluations accept the dissociation between initial performance and learning rate as well-supported by the data.

Strong agreement on claims C67-C71 regarding α-DTX occlusion experiments and Kv1.2 mechanism. OpenEval notes the occlusion experiment is strong but suggests direct Kv1.2 measurement would strengthen conclusions. Peer reviewers accepted the mechanism without challenge, with Reviewer 2 stating changes 'seem to be due to preferential reduction of Kv1.2 in dSPNs.'

Strong agreement on claims C89-C94, C96 regarding reversal learning deficits. Both evaluations find the behavioral dissociation between normal acquisition and impaired reversal well-characterized, with perseverative and regressive errors driving the deficit.

Strong agreement on claims C77-C80, C82-C83 regarding repetitive behaviors. Both evaluations accept increased grooming, marble burying, and nose poking as well-supported. Peer reviewers highlighted the machine learning-based Keypoint-MoSeq analysis as a particular strength.

Perfect agreement on claims C11, C117, C123-C124 regarding the correlative nature of physiology-behavior links. Both evaluations rate these as UNCERTAIN, noting the lack of causal manipulation experiments. Reviewer 2 explicitly stated findings are 'only correlative' and Reviewer 3 noted 'it is unclear whether this cellular phenotype alone can account for the behavioral alterations.'

Agreement on claims C56-C58, C63 regarding dSPN intrinsic excitability increases. OpenEval addresses C56-C58, C63 while peer review addresses broader set C56-C63. Both find evidence convincing. Peer reviewers called findings 'novel and valuable.'

Agreement on claims C104-C107, C109 regarding inconsistent prior literature on PV interneurons. Both evaluations accept the authors' summary of variable findings across studies and brain regions. Peer reviewers noted the striatal PV findings as 'novel and valuable.'

Partial agreement on synaptic findings. OpenEval R3 addresses claims C42-C45 (no synaptic changes), while peer R1 addresses broader set C5-C6, C39-C45 including both excitability and synaptic findings. Both find the negative synaptic results appropriately rule out synaptic mechanisms.

Partial agreement on increased spike probability in dSPNs. OpenEval R1 addresses claims C39-C40, C5 while peer R1 addresses broader set C5-C6, C39-C45. Both find the increased excitability in response to cortical stimulation well-supported with 'convincing' evidence.

Agreement on speculative nature of broader implications. OpenEval R14 addresses claims C125-C126 as explicitly speculative about generalization to other ASD models. Peer R8 addresses overlapping claims C11, C117, C123-C126 with focus on correlative nature. Both rate as UNCERTAIN, noting appropriate qualification by authors.

Agreement on claims C72-C73 regarding cell-type-specific α-DTX sensitivity. OpenEval R8 focuses on differential sensitivity between dSPNs and iSPNs. Peer R4 addresses broader Kv1.2 mechanism (C67-C73). Both accept the cell-type specificity as well-documented.

Agreement on claims C59-C60 regarding iSPN excitability trends. OpenEval R6 notes appropriate reporting of non-significant trend. Peer R3 addresses broader intrinsic excitability findings (C56-C63) including iSPN data. Both accept the cell-type specificity of the phenotype.

Agreement on claims C61-C62 regarding reduced AP latency in both cell types. OpenEval R17 notes this suggests some shared alterations alongside cell-type-specific effects. Peer R3 addresses broader intrinsic excitability set (C56-C63). Both accept the findings as supported.

Agreement on claims C84-C85 regarding behavioral rigidity measured by Keypoint-MoSeq. OpenEval R10 focuses on reduced entropy and syllable decoding. Peer R5 addresses broader repetitive behavior set (C7, C77-C85) and highlights machine learning analysis as a strength.

Agreement on claim C110 regarding lack of PV interneuron alterations in striatum. OpenEval R19 notes this is reasonable inference from comprehensive negative findings. Peer R11 addresses broader discussion (C104-C110) and calls striatal PV findings 'novel and valuable.'

Agreement on claim C41 regarding non-significant trend in iSPN spike probability. OpenEval R2 commends appropriate statistical interpretation of non-significant result. Peer R1 addresses broader set (C5-C6, C39-C45) but accepts all findings including the iSPN trend data.

OpenEval R20 addresses claims C111-C122 summarizing established literature on striatal function and providing context for behavioral findings. No corresponding peer review evaluation specifically addresses these background/discussion claims, though peer reviewers accepted the overall behavioral interpretations.
